items.title: Rift among organising Hindu groups: Two ‘Kumbh Melas’ now possible in Kerala in 2027
items.summary: ​Having successfully imported the grand scale of the North Indian Kumbh Mela to the banks of the Bharathapuzha in Malappuram district, the organisers of Kerala’s ‘Maha Magha Mahotsavam’ are now split. Festival committees of Thavanur and Thirunavaya, representing two banks of the river Bharathapuzha, who had been organising the event since 2016 and Varanasi’s Sri Panch Dasnam Juna Akhada, who made their entry in 2025 assuming a leadership role, are now locked in a bitter feud. The rift has been caused by concerns regarding financial transparency, and allegations of one-upmanship and sidelining of Kerala-based sanyasins against Juna Akhada’s Maha Mandaleshwar Swami Anandavanam Bharati. items.title: Bengaluru police book Conrad Hotel Management after electrocution deaths
items.summary: The Halasuru police have registered a case against the management of Conrad Hotel in Bengaluru for alleged negligence following the deaths of two foreign nationals in a suspected electrocution incident at the hotel's swimming pool on October 30. The incident, which occurred at the swimming pool on the third floor of the five-star hotel, also left two others injured while attempting to rescue the victims. The deceased have been identified as Alexander Maximilian Theiss (57), a German national and crew member of Lufthansa Airlines, and Juraj Horvat (45), a Slovakian national working as a project manager with IBM. The injured persons have been identified as Mathew Desantis (41), an American national staying at the hotel, and Rahul Tiwari (28), a hotel employee working as a pool attendant and lifeguard. Both sustained injuries while attempting to rescue the victims and were shifted to Manipal Hospital for treatment. According to the complaint filed by Silvia Hotuatova (47), wife of Horvat, the couple had arrived in India on October 20 for a holiday and checked into Conrad Hotel on October 30.
